articles.title: "Nikki did an STFU"- Veteran feels WWE is disrespecting John Cena by referencing past relationship on TV
articles.summary: John Cena has had many relationships, but the most publicized and documented was with WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella.
articles.body: John Cena has had many relationships, but the most publicized and documented was with WWE Hall of Famer Nikki Bella. The duo began dating in 2013 after Cena's first divorce and were together until 2018, when they split up and even called off their wedding. Despite it being eight years since then, WWE has been bringing up their relationship with major references on television over the last few weeks, and WWE veteran Jonathan Coachman found it disrespectful in regard to Cena.Jonathan Coachman says WWE is disrespecting John Cena by referencing him in Nikki Bella's feud on SmackDownNikki Bella has been involved in a heated feud with Paige ever since she betrayed her at WWE SummerSlam 2026. Over the last few months, Paige has mocked Bella about her past relationship with Cena. Moreover, in their latest singles match on the October 16 episode of SmackDown, Paige and Bella used Cena's moves on each other.Witnessing that, Jonathan Coachman called out WWE in the latest edition of The Coach and Bro Show. He said, "How long ago did Nikki Bella date and do that reality show with John Cena? Probably more than five years ago. Cena is either married or in a long-term relationship with a beautiful young lady that resembles Nikki Bella. So you put Nikki and Paige in a rivalry, and in the match, they do the ‘AAA,’ and the announcers say, ‘Clearly, that’s disrespecting because she dated Cena.’ Then Nikki did an STFU because that’s one of Cena’s moves."Why did John Cena and Nikki Bella break up?Despite being together for five years, living in the same house, and even John Cena proposing to Nikki Bella at WrestleMania 33, the couple parted ways. Nikki wanted children and marriage, while Cena was hesitant about both but still chose to marry her. However, he was and is still opposed to the idea of having kids. Following their separation, Cena married Shay Shariatzadeh, and Nikki tied the knot with her Dancing with the Stars choreographer, Artem Chigvintsev. However, they separated following a domestic violence and assault case in 2024.After her divorce, Nikki Bella returned to WWE in 2025 and has been a part-time star because of commitments outside the ring. articles.title: Abel Mansilla da otro paso contra el cáncer: 128 kilómetros en 24 horas por Extremadura
articles.standfirst: Será su séptimo gran desafío solidario, con los que ha recaudado cerca de 40.000 euros para la Asociación Española Contra el Cáncer
articles.summary: Será su séptimo gran desafío solidario, con los que ha recaudado cerca de 40.000 euros para la Asociación Española Contra el Cáncer.
articles.body: Abel Mansilla ya tiene la mirada puesta en su próximo desafío. Este deportista amateur, dedicado al entrenamiento personal, se prepara para caminar 128 kilómetros sin detenerse, con el objetivo de completar el recorrido en 24 horas. El 13 de noviembre partirá de Cáceres, a las 13.00 horas, para recorrer parte de la Vía de la Plata del Camino de Santiago y la Ruta Mozárabe. Pasará por Mérida y llegará al día siguiente a la plaza de España de Villanueva de la Serena, su tierra natal. Será su séptimo gran reto desde que, hace cinco años, se embarcara en estas aventuras extremas de la mano del grupo Pisadas Infinitas, con un propósito claro: recaudar fondos para la Asociación Española Contra el Cáncer (AECC). En este tiempo ha conseguido cerca de 40.000 euros. “Como reto benéfico es el último. Son 7 años pidiendo dinero a la gente y llega un punto en que ya me da apuro, pero seguiré con estos desafíos y dando visibilidad a la Asociación Española contra el Cáncer”, afirma Mansilla. Su historia con los desafíos de resistencia comenzó antes de darles un propósito solidario. Desde hace ocho años dirige Body&Mind, su centro de entrenamiento personal en Sanlúcar de Barrameda. Hace un tiempo abrió un canal de YouTube para compartir sus entrenamientos y, en uno de los vídeos, descubrió a otro preparador físico que había completado 24 horas caminando en Dubái. Aquella experiencia le motivó para empezar a publicar sus propios retos. Al principio fueron desafíos más modestos hasta que le propuso a su mujer ir caminando de Sanlúcar de Barrameda a Sevilla sin parar. A las 10 horas, una tromba de agua fue el preámbulo de un episodio febril que interrumpió su reto. Poco después, una compañera de trabajo de su mujer falleció de cáncer. Mansilla decidió entonces recuperar aquel desafío con fines benéficos y ayudar a la Asociación local contra el Cáncer, que atravesaba dificultades para recaudar fondos después de que la pandemia frenara sus actividades. Así nació, en 2021, su primer gran reto solidario. Caminó durante 24 horas seguidas por Sanlúcar de Barrameda, completó 118 kilómetros y recaudó 3.500 euros. La respuesta le animó a repetir la experiencia y convertirla en una cita periódica. En 2022 cruzó Fuerteventura de punta a punta sin detenerse. Fueron 105 kilómetros a pie durante 24 horas, con unas condiciones meteorológicas adversas, que se saldaron con una recaudación de 9.000 euros. Un año después volvió a multiplicar las dificultades. Primero afrontó un desafío vertical en el Hotel Guadalquivir, el edificio más alto de Sanlúcar de Barrameda, de 60 metros de altura. Completó 47 subidas y bajadas, acumuló diez kilómetros de desnivel vertical y sumó 17.860 escalones. En 2023 también recorrió durante 24 horas los pueblos blancos de la sierra de Cádiz, en una ruta circular que pasó por El Bosque, Grazalema, Benaocaz, Benamahoma, Villaluenga del Rosario y Ubrique. Aquella iniciativa permitió recaudar cerca de 3.000 euros. En 2024 se fijó en el faro de Chipiona, considerado el más alto de España. Durante 12 horas ininterrumpidas subió y bajó sus escaleras sin descanso. El reto se cerró con 3.300 euros. Su último reto no le dejó satisfecho. Volvió al Hotel Guadalquivir de Sanlúcar de Barrameda para batir su récord de subir y bajar las escaleras durante 24 horas. Cuando llevaba 14 en sus piernas, abandonó por problemas físicos. “El cuerpo me dio un aviso. Me jugó una mala pasada al sufrir una descompensación arterial tremenda. Tuve que parar”, recuerda Mansilla. Esta vez, Mansilla ha querido que el desafío le lleve hasta sus raíces. El recorrido de unos 128 kilómetros entre Cáceres y Villanueva de la Serena acumula alrededor de 900 metros de desnivel positivo. La distancia y el desnivel supondrán una exigencia importante, aunque él tiene claro que el mayor obstáculo será la noche. “Siempre lo es y no sólo por el sueño, pero al ser un reto en mi tierra, tendré a la familia cerca y eso siempre ayuda. Hay zonas que me las conozco bien, pero hay que tenerlo todo planificado en cuanto a suplementos de cafeína, hidratación y luego estar preparado para el frío y por si llueve”, analiza Mansilla. A menos de un mes de ponerse en marcha, ya piensa en el siguiente desafío. En 2027 podría afrontar el más ambicioso de su trayectoria: coronar de manera consecutiva la cima más alta de cada una de las ocho provincias andaluzas. El proyecto exigirá una planificación minuciosa y una gran capacidad de recuperación. Mansilla pretende completar el recorrido en régimen de autosuficiencia, de modo que el tiempo disponible para descansar, hidratarse, alimentarse y recuperarse entre montañas coincida con el necesario para desplazarse por carretera hasta la siguiente. Su itinerario incluiría el Mulhacén (3.479 metros), en Granada; el Chullo (2.611), en Almería; Pico Mágina (2.167), en Jaén; La Maroma o Pico Tejeda (2.066), en Málaga; El Torreón (1.654), en Cádiz; la Tiñosa (1.570), en Córdoba; El Terril, en Sevilla, y Los Bonales (1.055), en Huelva "Es plantearnos un nivel más en estos retos. Va a ser interesante a nivel físico y mental", apunta el extremeño que, a cada paso, demuestra que su esfuerzo puede dejar huella en los demás.

articles.title: Double gold, Games record! Nishad Kumar joins elite Indian club with historic Asian Para Games feat
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Nishad Kumar scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, winning his second gold medal in as many days to become only the third
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Nishad Kumar scripted history at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Tuesday, winning his second gold medal in as many days to become only the third Indian to claim two golds in a single edition of the continental para-sport showpiece.The two-time Paralympic silver medallist clinched the men's high jump T47 title with a Games-record effort of 2.04m in Aichi-Nagoya, a day after winning gold in the men's long jump T47 event with a best effort of 7.11m.Nishad's double-gold performance puts him in an elite club alongside Ankur Dhama and armless archer Sheetal Devi, who had both won two gold medals at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.Dhama won the men's 5000m T11 and 1500m T11 titles, while Sheetal struck gold in the women's individual compound open and mixed team compound open events.Nishad breaks Games record after long jump triumphKnown primarily for his high-jump exploits, Nishad demonstrated his versatility by adding the long jump crown to his collection before returning to his speciality on Tuesday.His 2.04m clearance secured the gold and established a new Games record in the men's high jump T47 category, which is meant for athletes with upper-limb impairments.The Indian's latest triumph adds to an impressive career that includes a silver medal at the Paris 2024 Paralympics and a world championship gold in the high jump.Nishad's journey has been marked by extraordinary resilience. His right arm was severed by a grass-cutting machine at his family's farm in Amb, Himachal Pradesh, when he was just six years old.PM Modi praises Nishad's versatility and determinationPrime Minister Narendra Modi had congratulated Nishad after his long jump gold on Monday, highlighting the significance of winning the event on his Asian Para Games debut."Very proud of Nishad Kumar on winning Gold in the Men’s Long Jump T47 event at the Asian Para Games 2026 with an outstanding jump. Winning a Gold on his debut in this event makes the achievement even more special. His versatility, determination and sporting excellence are truly inspiring. Wishing him the very best for the endeavours ahead," PM Modi was quoted as saying in a post by PMO India.The Prime Minister's message came after Nishad delivered a commanding performance in the long jump, recording 7.11m twice in the final.With two gold medals and a Games record, Nishad has emerged as one of India's standout performers in Aichi-Nagoya.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Jalen Brunson's mom, Sandra, writes him a letter before his first game as an NBA champion.
articles.summary: Before every game, Jalen Brunson's mom, Sandra, sends him a text message. Before his first game as an NBA Champion, she did something a little different.
articles.body:
It feels like yesterday that I was 25, working as a paralegal in New York City up at 30 Rockefeller Plaza, and pregnant with my baby boy. Your dad was playing basketball in Australia at the time, and he'd begged me to come with him for the season. But I was stubborn. I knew I didn't want to have my baby in another country ... so I stayed home, and you were born in New Jersey. And you were perfect.

I was lucky as a new mom, where even with your dad overseas I still had a lot of help. Your grandparents were always around, and they loved to spoil you. I remember those first two weeks, you literally doubled your weight. Like you got so chubby that I was WORRIED! But you grew into it. As soon as you could walk, your dad put a basketball in your hands ... and as soon as you had one in your hands, you wouldn't let it go. We'd be eating breakfast, eating dinner, working around the house ... and no matter what, you'd be over there on the floor, just dribbling that ball. I tried to tell everyone it's too much....... I was like, Enough already!!! He can't do this all day every day. But whenever I'd try, your grandfather would just give me this look. And then in his thick Jamaican accent he'd say, "Let him bum di ball . Let him bum di ball . Let him bum di ball . It's fine ."

So I let you do your thing ... and you kept bummin' di ball . Sometimes it got us into trouble. I remember at one of your dad's first home games with the Knicks, when you were three, we were in the family room at the Garden and you were dribbling up and down the floor. Everyone thought it was so cute ... but not me. I knew what a demon you could be with that basketball. So I was trying to smile, while in truth I was beyond nervous. I mean, Jeff Van Gundy's wife was there, Allan Houston's wife ... it was everyone. And they're all egging you on and of course you're loving it. Until you take one too many dribbles, and the ball goes SPLAT right onto a table, right on someone's plate, and their food is flying everywhere. At the time, since we were new, I was so embarrassed! But I look back on those moments now, and I see them for what they actually were - what every moment has always been when you have a basketball in your hands: pure joy.

It's like that saying goes, "Find a job you love, and you'll never work a day in your life." Except I think you may have taken it to heart a little sooner than you're supposed to. Because you didn't just fall in love with the sport of basketball as a kid..... you also fell in love with the job of being a basketball player . I always laugh when I think about you at five, six years old, mimicking your dad and his teammates. Whether it was perfecting Allan Houston's jab step, or Larry Johnson's "Big L" celebration ... or it was making me cut your t-shirt sleeves into the "muscle shirts" that Knicks players were wearing back then, or cut my trouser socks into tiny armbands ... or it was packing a duffel bag filled with Gatorade bottles, sneakers and a uniform, just like the one your dad would leave with on game days, so you could "leave" for your own games (in the house or on the driveway) ... you always had such an attention to detail.

But it wasn't just that cute stuff. I remember when you were in kindergarten, your dad was on the Blazers, so his games would usually start at around 10:00 p.m. our time. You didn't care. You refused to sleep until you'd not only watched the game (had to be live), but also talked to your dad and given him notes. "You missed this shot," "you made a nice pass here," whatever you'd noticed. And when you could be at his games in person, all you ever wanted was to be chasing rebounds, folding towels, getting water for the players, helping out in some way. I'll never forget when you were in fourth or fifth grade, we were living in South Jersey at the time, and one of your classmates had Sixers tickets and he asked if you wanted to go. You said no thanks. I thought to myself, That's such a nice offer...... why doesn't Jalen want to go?? And it was at that moment that I realized something: You didn't want to attend a basketball game just to sit in the stands. If you were going to be around it, you wanted to be a part of it . You wanted to work . And as I think back on your journey now, I'm struck by how deep your sense of PURPOSE has been ... how you've always known exactly what you want out of the game.

And how you've always been willing to work for it, so you've never been willing to settle for less.

I've also been thinking a lot lately about my favorite tradition of ours.

It started when you were a sophomore in high school.... Dad got a coaching opportunity with the Bobcats, so he was moving to North Carolina for the season. And I knew how much you were gonna miss him, especially on game days. So I wanted you to have a little extra support in those moments. Which led me to an idea: The night before every game, I would type up some words of encouragement on the computer and print them out. Then the next morning, before you woke up, I'd tape the message to your bathroom mirror, and the refrigerator, and even put a copy in your lunchbag ... any place where you could reflect on the words I chose. And eventually that just became our pregame ritual.

We kept it going throughout high school.......... and what a high school career you had. Leading Stevenson to its first-ever boys' basketball state championship as a senior!!!

But I think your college career is when the tradition really took on a new meaning. Our family decided to move east to be nearer to you at Villanova, but I'd stayed behind at first to close out our house back in Illinois. Which meant that when I got to see you play college ball for the first time during that preseason, you'd already been there for a couple of months. And while I barely remember what happened in that game, I remember talking to you after. I think I mentioned a tough call that didn't go your way, or some missed free throws where you'd looked frustrated, or something like that. And your response ... whew ... it really stuck with me. You sort of slouched your shoulders a bit, and you said, "Mom........ not you, too."

As soon as you said that, it was like this lightbulb moment for me as a parent ... where I realized, you're hearing it from EVERYONE now when it comes to the basketball stuff. Your dad, your coaches, fans, haters, media, social media. So the last thing you needed was to also hear it from me. And from that point forward I said to myself, No rehashing anything that happened on the court. What he needs from me is simply to BE THERE for him. As his mom. And after that, not to brag..... but I think you and I kind of locked in. We had to switch from printouts to texts, of course, since you weren't living at home anymore. But we figured it out. And (give or take a few delays, and a few close calls!!!) I've texted you ahead of every game you've played in since.

One thing I love about our tradition, Jalen, it's how I can trace the entire journey you've been on over these last 15 years, just from the themes of what I've written to you. Like in high school, I felt so protective ... with you being highly touted, opposing players and coaches would often talk about how, If we stop Brunson, we're good. So I'd send you quotes on teamwork, as a reminder that basketball is a team sport, and it's never all on you. In college, you became such a brilliant leader ... so I'd keep it simple, with messages like, Good luck, son, LEAD your team to victory!!! Then when you got to the NBA, suddenly you weren't in a leadership role anymore ... and there were times where you might not even play!! So my messages were more about showing patience, having discipline, and remembering your love for the game. Then your last year in Dallas ... let's just say ... a theme from those messages was "knowing your worth." And your first year in New York? I guess I went full Mama Bear, keeping every receipt from all the people questioning your contract, or doubting you could be a star.

Finally, in June ... I almost still can't believe it ... I got to send you NBA FINALS texts! And in the best way possible, those texts felt like a culmination of everything that had come before.

We take one possession, one quarter, one half, and one GAME at a time. You and your teammates had to wait to find out your opponent ... and with that comes patience, discipline and confidence. Confidence that you can handle whatever comes your way. When they make it about you, make it about the team. Play YOUR game........ When you control the pace, your teammates thrive off of your energy. Find a way and leave no doubt.

June 10th, before Game 4 in New York ... and after a certain shove:

When your opponent tries to bring out the worst in you, you rise above and get the job done. We find a way.

And last but not least ... June 13th, before Game 5 ... the night you guys made history:

Good luck tonight, son..... There is much to be said about this opportunity. Every time you take the court is another opportunity. You and your team can seize this moment ... and may it live on forever!!! Leave no doubt.

I'll tell you about one other text message ... this time, one I received. It was from my fellow NBA mom and friend, Linda Shanklin, who most people will know as Andre Iguodala's mom. She sent it the day after you guys won the championship, to congratulate me on everything. And she gave me a piece of advice, as someone who'd been through this experience before. She told me to savor and enjoy your accomplishment ... and that October will arrive quicker than I can imagine. I remember reading her message at the time, and that last part not fully registering with me. But of course she was right. I feel like I blinked, and the summer flew by...... and now it's about to be Opening Night.

And I guess I wanted to write you this, Jalen, because I know what your nature is. You take your responsibilities so seriously, and you're so dedicated to your work. After the celebration ended in June, I actually think our first conversation wasn't even about your amazing victory ... it was you asking me a logistics question about your youth camp in Chicago later that month! So I know that your instinct is always going to be to get back to business...... and I know that as soon as the season starts, you're going to be focused on bringing Knicks fans another championship. But you're still my baby boy, so you still have to listen to me. And I'm pulling the Mom Card on this one, and demanding that you let yourself enjoy the moment tonight. This is NOT just another game day...... which is why I'm not just sending you another pregame text.

Because tonight, you'll be playing basketball for the first time as an NBA champion.

It's funny, but I remember when you signed with the Knicks, one of the things that people would say about you is that you were some kind of "nepo baby." (I told you, Mama Bear kept receipts!) That somehow your dad had gotten you a job with the team. And I always thought that it was ironic in a way. Because the truth is, for all the fond memories I have of the Garden, and of your dad's time there..... I won't lie: That was a stressful time. I won't try to claim we were struggling. We were very fortunate, and had a lot more than most. But being a journeyman, or the family of a journeyman, is not an easy basketball life. You're living contract to contract ... you're moving around constantly ... you're spending months apart ... there are just so many little uncertainties that come with trying to make it on the margins of the league. So when I said that I was "nervous" in the Knicks' family room back then, I wasn't joking! We were never anywhere long enough to not feel nervous.

But if there's a silver lining to life on the margins, it's that you find out who people really are ... because there's less for them to gain from treating you well. And there were so many people in New York who treated us well. Treated us like family, to be honest. We walked into that family room, and you might as well have been the son of the franchise player! Like, I swear ... not once did I have to show a credential when I was there with you. There was genuine kindness for us. And I'll tell you something about being a mom..... When someone shows kindness to your kid? You never forget it.

So it's hard for me to even put in words, Jalen, how gratifying it's been to watch as you've come into full bloom over these last few years. And how meaningful it is to me that you've done it in that building, with that team, for that city.

I'm not sure if I've ever told you this ... but your first season after you signed with the Knicks in free agency, it was surreal. It was like every time I'd go to the Garden to watch you play, I would reconnect with someone from our past. Former players, employees who were still with the team, fans who'd been there since the '90s. And every conversation always went the same. They would tell me, not just how they're so happy a player helped bring the magic back to the Garden ... but how they're so happy it was JALEN. I shed tears during some of those conversations, that's how moved I was by them. I'll probably shed tears after sending you this letter. And I'll warn you up front: I'm definitely shedding tears at your ring ceremony on Opening Night. What can I say?? It's been that kind of journey.

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Devender Kumar strikes gold as India sweep historic 1-2-3 finish in men's discus throw
articles.summary: India scripted a memorable podium sweep at the Asian Para Games, with Devender Kumar, Rakesh and Pardeep Kumar claiming gold, silver and bronze,
articles.body: India scripted a memorable podium sweep at the Asian Para Games, with Devender Kumar, Rakesh and Pardeep Kumar claiming gold, silver and bronze, respectively, in the men's discus throw F43/F44/F62/F64 final. Devender led the Indian charge with 781 Raza points, while Rakesh finished second with 771 points. Pardeep completed the clean sweep with 669 points, despite recording the longest throw of the competition.Devender's second-round effort seals goldDevender secured gold with a best effort of 49.71 metres in his second attempt. After opening with 48.85m, he fouled on his third and fourth throws, managed 45.20m in the fifth, and recorded another foul in his final attempt. His second-round effort ultimately proved decisive.Rakesh claimed silver with 771 points after recording a best throw of 49.35m in his fourth attempt. He began with 47.87m before registering 46.08m in the second round and fouling on his third attempt. articles.title: Week 7 Fantasy Football Waiver Wire: Rookies Mike Washington Jr., Omar Cooper Jr. among top pickups
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his recommendations at each position off the fantasy football waiver wire for Week 7.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

It's not a great week for fantasy quarterback options, which isn't great news for managers in search of bye-week replacements for Josh Allen, Trevor Lawrence and Jayden Daniels.

There's always the usual crop from streamers listed below, as well as a potential new starter in J.J. McCarthy, who flashed after Jameis Winston was benched. However, I'll remind everyone that Mayfield is expected to return this week.

While his early-season results left a lot to be desired, a healthy Mayfield is in the mix as a fantasy starter. The veteran is one year removed from averaging the fifth-most fantasy points among passers in 2024. He also managed QB15 stats during an injury-riddled 2025 campaign for the Bucs offense. Mayfield also has a softer schedule coming up, with the Panthers, Falcons, Bears, a bye, Lions and Panthers again. All of those defenses rank inside the top half of the league in fantasy points allowed to QBs.

Kyler Murray is 51% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

Risky streaming options (if starter is out)

Desperation streaming options (if named starter)

Ashton Jeanty and Klint Kubiak professed all week long that the Raiders' starting running back was finally healthy after battling ankle issues in the opening month. Given the good matchup with the Bills, it seemed like the perfect springboard to a strong fantasy outing.

Unfortunately, Jeanty struggled with efficiency once again, managing just 22 yards on 10 carries, while adding another 36 yards on four receptions. A touchdown saved his fantasy day, but he was held under 60% of the snaps for the second straight week.

Meanwhile, Washington played a season-high 35% of the snaps and turned his 10 touches into 50 scrimmage yards. That was aided by Jeanty getting only limited playing time in the second half, which was strange considering the game was tied 13-13 at halftime.

Despite their claims of Jeanty's health last week, it doesn't seem like the 22-year-old is playing at 100%. It's unclear if the team will consider resting him, the same way the Cardinals did with Jeremiyah Love in Week 6, but it's a possibility.

Either way, Washington needs to be rostered everywhere. Not only is he the next man up in Vegas, he's also looked good with the volume he's been given. The rookie is currently an RB3/flex option with top-15 upside if Jeanty ever misses time.

The Saints' backfield has been a frustrating three-man committee all season, regardless of which backs are healthy. Fortunately, we might have some clarity for Week 7.

Alvin Kamara has battled injuries the last two games and simply can't handle a significant workload at 31 years old. He's settled into more of a complementary pass-catching role, which he's splitting with CJ Donaldson.

That left Miller with the majority of the early-down work, resulting in a season-high 20 carries and 70 yards in a positive game script Sunday against the Giants. Miller also has two touchdowns on the year.

Travis Etienne Jr. won't be available to return from injured reserve until after the team's Week 8 bye, so we'll get at least one more game with the current trio. That makes Miller a high-end RB3 with RB2 upside against the Steelers. Kamara should only be viewed as a risky flex option.

We don't know if Cam Skattebo's sudden disappearance from the offense will continue or whether it was a one-game punishment . But considering the team's interest in other running backs this offseason, it doesn't seem like they view Skattebo as a meaningful piece of the offense.

The committee approach in Week 6 didn't exactly solve the Giants' woes in the rushing attack. Devin Singletary played 40% of the snaps and turned five touches into 33 yards. Najee Harris failed to make a dent with just 2 yards on four carries and was cut from the roster on Tuesday.

Tracy made the most noise from a fantasy perspective, generating 45 yards and two scores on eight touches and a 38% snap share. There was no doubt he had the most juice from this group, so now we'll wait to see if the coaches felt the same way.

Remember, Tracy topped 1,000 scrimmage yards in each of the past two seasons. He's more than capable of leading this backfield if he gets the chance. I highly recommend stashing him and monitoring the situation.

If Coleman was dropped, you should be stashing him in your IR spot. J.K. Dobbins has found the end zone in each of the past two games, but he hasn't played well this season. RJ Harvey has also failed to make a case for the lead back role.

Meanwhile, Coleman flashed with 58 yards, three catches and a touchdown the last time he was on the field. The rookie is a no-risk investment that could pay off in a big way in the second half of the season, especially if Dobbins' durability issues return.

This is an extreme long shot, but Conner is a potential trade candidate who's sitting on IR in Arizona. I have the veteran stashed in several leagues, just in case the Cardinals send him to an RB-needy roster before the deadline.

Rachaad White is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 RB add, if available. Just note that he is on bye in Week 7.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Risky flex options (if healthy and starter is out)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

The Jets' offense has been a revolving door with injuries to Cooper, Adonai Mitchell, Kenyon Sadiq, Mason Taylor and Breece Hall in the first five weeks. However, Cooper has made the most of his opportunities when he's been on the field.

The rookie played five snaps in the opener before getting hurt, but came away with a 30-yard catch in his debut. After spending a month on IR, he returned this week with a six-catch, 103-yard, one-touchdown effort on seven targets in a full-time role. He also had a second TD called back on a penalty.

Whenever a first-round wideout is immediately productive, fantasy managers should take notice. Mitchell is still week-to-week after undergoing surgery on his finger. Even when he returns, it's impossible to push Cooper aside based on what he's put on tape so far.

The Jets also have some favorable matchups in the next month, including the Dolphins, Raiders and Bills in three of their next four outings. Don't overlook Cooper's performance, he's a must-add to see if he can keep this up.

Lane is in a similar situation to Cooper, as a rookie who got hurt in the opener and returned from IR with a solid performance in Week 6.

Lane caught only one of his three targets (though Lamar Jackson was looking for him in the end zone) before fracturing his wrist in Week 1. Thankfully, he made a full recovery and, on Sunday, began to show why the Ravens used a third-round pick on him in April.

The 22-year-old earned five targets against the Browns, finishing with four receptions and 40 yards while catching passes from backup Tyler Huntley. Rashod Bateman suffered a shoulder injury in the game, which could sidelined him for multiple weeks, depending on the severity.

With Jackson expected back, possibly as soon as this week, Baltimore's passing attack will be a much more dangerous unit. That's important since they'll be squaring off in potential shootouts with the Bengals, Bills and Jaguars over the next three games.

Lane might not have the same draft capital investment as Cooper, but there's a path to him emerging as a fantasy WR3/flex option in Declan Doyle's scheme.

Antonio Williams/Treylon Burks, Commanders

Terry McLaurin was carted off Monday night with a significant knee injury that's likely going to sideline him for a while. That opens the door for Williams to emerge as a consistent weapon in the Commanders offense.

The third-round rookie actually led Washington's receivers in snaps and routes run in the loss to the 49ers, finishing the game with 50 yards on three receptions. We've also seen him flash multiple times in the first six weeks, including a four-catch, 64-yard, one-touchdown debut and an 87-yard TD in Week 4 that was called back due to a penalty.

Williams could be just as valuable as Cooper and Lane in terms of waiver wire pickups, you'll just need to stash him on your bench while he's on bye this week.

In deeper formats, you can also consider Burks, who stepped up in McLaurin's absence with four catches and 66 yards. He's also scored a pair of touchdowns this season. However, he walked off late in Monday's game with trainers and we might not get an update on his status until the team returns for their Week 8 matchup with the Eagles.

Noel is finally showing the world what he can do as a consistent part of the Texans' offense. The sophomore receiver has at least 50 yards and/or a touchdown in four of his six appearances this season, while only playing 62% of Houston's snaps or less in every game.

The 24-year-old is on a three-game hot streak at the moment with stat lines of 3-85-0, 5-41-1, and 4-107-1 on Sunday.

The Texans have found very little success on the ground this season and with the arrival of Marvin Harrison Jr. and how well C.J. Stroud is playing, it makes complete sense for them to take to the air more.

Nico Collins, MHJ and Noel can form a very threatening trio, but don't discount Noel's potential production in that group. He's a WR4/flex with some upside and should benefit from defenses focusing on his more well-known teammates.

We know the deal with Tucker, so fantasy managers should understand how to value him by now. He can't be trusted as a consistent weekly producer, but when bye weeks and injuries hit your lineup, you can absolutely start him as a home-run swing.

We've seen him deliver on two occasions this year, a five-catch, 119-yard, one-touchdown performance in Week 2 against the Chargers and a five-catch, 97-yard, two-score afternoon versus the Bills on Sunday. Those also happen to be his two easiest opponents this season, so keep that in mind.

You don't need to break the bank to acquire Tucker, but if you're searching the waiver wire for someone who can help you overcome a deficit, he's a strong spot start in the right matchups. If you just need a steady high-floor, low-ceiling WR4/flex, then you could consider Malik Washington instead.

Germie Bernard is 50% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Jordyn Tyson is 48% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Bernard, if available.

Jakobi Meyers is 47% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Bernard and Tyson, if available. Just note that he is on bye in Week 7.

Alec Pierce is 51% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

The Rams' offense is about to look a lot different with Davante Adams sidelined six to 10 weeks due to a ruptured hamstring . Puka Nacua is already getting as much volume as he can handle, but the team will need to max him out every way possible now. While receiver Konata Mumpfield will take on some of Adams' targets (and can be added as a flex option), the tight ends will become an even more valuable part of this attack.

In the short term, that means Tyler Higbee will be a strong streaming option in Week 7. The veteran went over 60 yards in three straight games, before a quieter stat line in Sunday's loss.

Beyond that, Ferguson becomes very intriguing as a rest-of-season fantasy asset. The second-year tight end is currently on IR until Week 8, so fantasy managers will need to be patient. However, the upside is hard to ignore.

Ferguson has scored a touchdown in each of the four full games he's played when either Nacua or Adams sat out. One of those contests occurred earlier this season, when he posted six catches for 54 yards and a score on nine targets.

Though it's possible an aggressive organization like the Rams makes a trade for a receiver to replace Adams, Ferguson is still a priority stash with a clear path to becoming a fantasy TE1 as Matthew Stafford's No. 2 pass-catcher until Adams returns.

It's been a bizarre stretch for Hockenson the last three weeks, starting with him hauling in all 13 of his targets in Week 4 en route to a 119-yard day against the Dolphins. He wasn't able to repeat that effort because he suffered a concussion in Week 5 after just two snaps.

Now, coming off the bye week, Hockenson should be ready to roll in a very friendly matchup with a floundering Colts franchise. Indy has also been lit up by several tight ends this season, including 9-101-1 to Travis Kelce and 5-44-2 to Pat Freiermuth.

A week later, Hockenson will take on a Lions defense allowing the most fantasy points to tight ends. So at worst, you can start him as a high-end TE2 streamer in those games.

Terry McLaurin's injury also frees up more targets for Okonkwo, who is finally back to playing a normal snap share after missing time with a hamstring injury in the opening month.

Over the last two weeks, Okonkwo has put up 60 yards on six targets versus the Giants and 69 yards on seven targets against the 49ers.

Prior to the arrival of Stefon Diggs, Okonkwo was one of my favorite sleepers this summer. With McLaurin expected to miss extended time, the 27-year-old tight end is once again set up to challenge for low-end fantasy TE1 value rest of season.

This is the third Raider that I've written about in this column, which probably sets a new record. However, there's value to be found in an offense that's been competitive this season with Klint Kubiak leading the way in Vegas.

Mayer isn't your traditional No. 2 tight end, because Brock Bowers plays more of a receiver role in the offense. You could argue that Mayer is actually the starting tight end in this offense and the results have been there more often than not in the last month with 32 yards and a touchdown in Week 3, 82 yards in Week 4 and 95 yards on Sunday.

Tucker is a boom-or-bust receiver, so you can expect this passing attack to operate through Bowers and Mayer most weeks. That puts Mayer on the TE2 streamer radar with a higher ceiling than most players in that range, who are just TD-dependent.

Hunter Henry is 51% rostered but would be the No. 1 TE add, if available.

Pat Freiermuth is 46% rostered but would be the No. 2 TE add behind Henry, if available.

Will Reichard is 59% rostered but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Quarterbacks: Jalen Hurts, Bo Nix, Justin Herbert

Running Backs: MarShawn Lloyd, David Montgomery, Kenny Gainwell, Keaton Mitchell

Wide Receivers: Josh Downs, Chris Godwin Jr., Cortland Sutton, Michael Pittman Jr.

Tight Ends: Mark Andrews, Jake Ferguson, Dalton Schultz

MarShawn Lloyd got hurt and failed to come through in what might be his final start for the Packers. With Josh Jacobs expected to return this week, Lloyd goes back to being a one-injury-away backup and given how he performed in the last six weeks, he doesn't need to be stashed unless you're in a very deep league.

When Josh Downs posted back-to-back 70-plus yard games in Week 2 and Week 3, it appeared he might have a chance to unlock a new ceiling the rest of the way with Alec Pierce sidelined. Unfortunately, he's failed to reach 50 yards in any game since and has settled into the low-ceiling flex territory for fantasy. A matchup with the Vikings defense in Week 7 isn't going to help his outlook.

Mark Andrews hasn't topped 50 yards in a game this year and has been held under 30 yards in each of the past three weeks. The veteran is just a TD-or-bust fantasy TE2, who has only one score on the season.

articles.title: Fallece Gustavo Oliva, referente en el pádel, dejando un emotivo mensaje: “Solo puedo dar las gracias”
articles.standfirst: El exjugador y entrenador compartió una publicación en redes sociales antes de perder la vida a causa de un cáncer de colon
articles.summary: El exjugador y entrenador compartió una publicación en redes sociales antes de perder la vida a causa de un cáncer de colon
articles.body: La peor de las noticias ha golpeado al pádel nacional. Gustavo Oliva, un referente de este deporte tanto en España como en Cataluña, ha fallecido a los 58 años de edad debido a un cáncer de colon. El exjugador y profesor fue uno de los grandes impulsores del gran crecimiento que ha vivido el pádel en los últimos años y, pese al dolor del suceso, dejó un emotivo mensaje en sus redes sociales en el que mostraba su agradecimiento por todo lo vivido. Gustavo, como tantos otros, empezó jugando al tenis. Posteriormente se pasó al pádel y llegó a convertirse en uno de los mejores jugadores del país. Incluso llegó a capitanear la selección catalana durante varios años. Lo compaginó con sus clases como entrenador, fundando también la Padel Academy de Barcelona. Toda una figura dentro del país y especialmente en su zona, en la Ciudad Condal. A los 52 años le detectaron dos tumores enormes y metástasis en el bazo y el hígado en un análisis que, según reconoce, debía haberse hecho antes. Tenía cáncer de colon y los médicos le daban como mucho tres años más de vida. No obstante, Gustavo consiguió alargar el diagnóstico hasta que el pasado lunes 19 de octubre, a los 58 años de edad, falleció. Oliva tenía dos hijas, de 30 y 33 años, y estaba felizmente casado. Así pues, antes de morir, el exjugador compartió una publicación en sus redes en la que compartía varias reflexiones y agradecimientos antes de irse: “Mi vida en la Tierra llega a su fin en breve. Irte con 58 años en nuestros tiempos y nuestro entorno es pronto, pero a lo largo de los años he aprendido a ver la vida con perspectiva y eso me hace ver lo afortunado que soy de haber vivido una vida muy completa y feliz y eso me ayuda a marchar con una paz y tranquilidad que ni yo nunca me hubiera imaginado”. Gustavo quiso tener también unas bonitas palabras hacia sus seres allegados: “Solo puedo dar las gracias a mi entorno. Mi familia me quiere muchísimo y me he intentado rodear de unas amistades de las cuales me siento muy afortunado. He aprendido a tener relación con quien estás a gusto, te quiere y te hace sentir tal cual como eres. Por eso me siento tan feliz y afortunado. Muchísimas gracias familia, muchísimas gracias amigos”. Además, dio una importante lección: “Por si ayuda nunca a alguien, quisiera recordar la importancia de las revisiones médicas y de la prevención. También he tenido la suerte de tener una vida llena de salud, sin ningún contratiempo importante y pudiendo disfrutar al máximo en cada momento. Quizás por ello y por el exceso de confianza no seguí unas normas básicas de prevención y cuando empecé a notar los primeros síntomas, ya tenía un enorme cáncer colorrectal con metástasis en hígado, bazo y numerosos ganglios. Siguiendo la prevención aconsejada, seguro que se hubiera detectado a tiempo”. Cerrando con una despedida que emociona: “Hasta siempre familia. Hasta siempre amigos”. La publicación tuvo muchas reacciones de varias de las figuras más importantes de la historia de este deporte, como es el caso de Fernando Belasteguín: “La comida pendiente que nos prometíamos en los últimos mensajes la haremos cuando nos volvamos a encontrar, porque lo haremos. Te mando un fuerte abrazo para vos y tu familia”. Al igual que Carolina Navarro: “Tus palabras me dan tranquilidad y, sobre todo, la sensación de que has vivido una vida feliz”. También ha escrito otros como Maxi Grabiel, Willy Lahoz, Alex Corretja, Toni Bueno o Fer Poggi. Sin embargo, las reacciones más especiales llegaban de parte de sus hijas, que también compartieron sus mensajes en redes sociales: “El mejor padre del mundo y la persona más admirable, te amo por siempre, papi”. Importantes organizaciones en las que tuvo mucho peso como la Federación Catalana también han hecho un comunicado en el que expresan su dolor por la pérdida: “Gustavo formó parte del pádel catalán desde sus inicios y nuestro deporte tuvo un peso muy grande en su vida. Jugador del circuito catalán y de la selección catalana, entrenador y, sobre todo, un gran referente para todos nosotros”. Una persona muy valiosa dentro del pádel nacional que se marcha dejando grandes recuerdos, un importante legado tras de sí, una bonita despedida y una importante lección de vida.

articles.title: Ballard’s Firing Could Put DeForest Buckner on Detroit’s Radar
articles.summary: Chris Ballard's firing has DeForest Buckner looking available, and Detroit has a real reason to call. #OnePride
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday , and it could lead to the team trading away several players at the trade deadline, including defensive tackle DeForest Buckner . Buckner did not hide his frustration after Sunday's loss to the Tennessee Titans, telling reporters, "I'm sick and tired of the same song and dance every year," in a postgame session posted by reporter James Boyd .

There is already trade interest for him. "Could the 49ers work it out? Could they get him for half a season? I don't know. I would think so. Why not? DeForest Buckner is one of the most solid players you'll ever see. He's entirely team-oriented [and] a workhorse. He's a pillar of a locker room," Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area said on an Oct. 18 livestream on her YouTube channel , a day before Ballard was let go.

With Buckner being on an expiring contract, would the Detroit Lions make a call to Indianapolis about him? Even though the defensive line has been much improved for Detroit this season, adding Buckner to a group that could still use help would not hurt them.

DeForest Buckner Would Be a Heavy Cap Hit for a Rental

Buckner has a base salary of $13 million for the 2026 season, and his cap hit is $26.6 million. Spotrac also lists him as an unrestricted free agent in 2027, so this is the last year of the deal. Whoever trades for him is buying a half-season rental, not a long-term piece. Buckner is 32 years old. If the Lions are going to trade for him, it might cost general manager Brad Holmes a second-round pick in order to get him.

Detroit is a team that is in win-now mode, and it could still improve the defensive line. In six games this season, he has recorded 26 tackles, four sacks, one fumble recovery, and three pass deflections .

The Bears Are the Reason Brad Holmes Should Call

Even though San Francisco could be interested in reuniting with Buckner, the real reason why Detroit should get him is because it would be hard to believe that Ryan Poles and the Chicago Bears wouldn't try to make a move for him.

Chicago is no doubt going to try to improve the interior of the defensive line. The Bears are also in win-now mode with Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson. If the Lions added Buckner in a trade, it would be a big help because it could take some pressure off of Aidan Hutchinson.

Even if the Lions were to trade away a second-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft for Buckner, they could still use a later-round pick to trade for a cornerback, whether that would be for Sauce Gardner, Riq Woolen, Zyon McCollum, or someone else.

Buckner being traded back to San Francisco potentially could make sense for both parties. If that doesn't occur, Holmes and the Lions need to do whatever it takes to acquire him, in order that it doesn't potentially make Chicago's defense better.

articles.title: Panthers' Brady Tkachuk Plans to Donate Any Jerseys Senators Fans Throw on Ice to Charity
articles.summary: Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk says he already has plans for what he'll do with any jerseys disgruntled Ottawa Senators throw on the ice during their former captain's Wednesday night homecoming.
articles.body:
Florida Panthers forward Brady Tkachuk says he already has plans for what he'll do with any jerseys disgruntled Ottawa Senators throw on the ice during their former captain's Wednesday night homecoming.

"Just talking with our team, and gonna be talking with the Boys and Girls Club, that every jersey that gets thrown on the ice is going to get donated to a friend at the Boys and Girls Club in Ottawa," Tkachuk said around the 14:10 mark of Tuesday's Wingmen podcast with his brother and teammate Matthew Tkachuk.

"So, I don't recommend doing it, but... if you're going to do it, and send a message, just know it's going to a good cause. I receive your message, and it's going to a good cause. I almost appreciate it."

Tkachuk served as captain of the Senators for five seasons prior to his June trade to the Panthers. The move came shortly after the Senators lost in the first round of the playoffs for a second straight season.

Senators general manager Steve Staios later said Tkachuk had requested a trade and leveraged his no-move clause in order to land with the Panthers.

Tkachuk's brother went through his own split with a Canadian team four years ago. Matthew played six seasons with the Calgary Flames before informing the team he wouldn't sign an extension prior to his 2022 trade to the Panthers.

Matthew noted on the podcast his return to Calgary had less of an impact in part because the game featured teams from opposite conferences.

Brady's return to Ottawa, on the other hand, represents a divisional matchup for two teams heading into Wednesday neck-and-neck in the Atlantic standings.

"It's nice for me, too, because I'm just going to focus on that," Tkachuk said. "It is an intra-divisional game. Is it a big game individually? Yes. But it's a bigger game for our team. That's a four-point swing. I know that's going to be my focus of a distraction away from all the other stuff."

Wednesday's homecoming, which Tkachuk said he was "going to be nervous" for, comes just as the Panthers are heating up despite losing Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov to injury during the early stretch of the season.

Tkachuk has scored nine points in his last three games while becoming the third player in NHL history to record natural hat tricks in consecutive games. That has helped the Panthers stack three straight wins heading into this week's four-game road swing.

Tkachuk isn't the only former captain preparing for a potentially dramatic return to his former home arena this week. Former Vancouver Canucks star Quinn Hughes is preparing to come back to Rogers Arena this Sunday for the first time since he was traded last December to the Minnesota Wild.

articles.title: Mark Allen: Snooker star suggests career could be over after losing in first round of Northern Ireland Open in Belfast
articles.summary: "I've been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don't see a future with snooker in it, if I'm honest" - Mark Allen in a "bad place" and admits his career could be over after losing to Jordan Brown in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast
articles.body:
Allen was playing his first match since his world championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April, when he missed a match-ball black off the spot at 16-15 in front and went on to lose a decider.

The 40-year-old has since stayed away from the tour due to personal issues that he has kept private but are understood not to relate to any repercussions from the manner of his defeat at the Crucible.

After his 4-2 defeat to Jordan Brown, a close friend and compatriot who is also from Antrim, Allen indicated he is set to take another long and potentially permanent break from the sport.

In an emotional interview with TNT Sports , Allen said he was "really overwhelmed", adding: "I'm in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough.

"I think if I wasn't playing Jordan I wouldn't have come back. I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates, I thought that was a better way to sign out."

Asked if he was serious about his threat to retire, Allen confirmed his view and continued: "I've been flooded with support but the problems are within. I just don't see a future with snooker in it, if I'm honest.

"It's sad to say, because it's all I've loved to do since I was 12 but the last few months has been really difficult and it's put snooker into perspective for me. At the minute I'm just trying to survive."

Allen has won both UK and Masters titles in a total of 12 ranking tournament wins, and has reached the world championship semi-finals three times.

Brown said: "First and foremost it's just great to see Mark back playing. He obviously came through a tough time off the table and I'm with him every step of the way, like everybody is.

"We're all behind him. I miss him and I love him and we all just want to see him healthy and well and playing the game that he loves so much. He's a great player and a great guy."

Both World Snooker Tour and the sport's governing body, the WPBSA, have provided support to Allen and have indicated their desire to continue helping him in any way they can.

articles.title: NFL Injury Report, Week 7: Latest news, updates for Davante Adams, Mike Evans, Lamar Jackson, more players
articles.summary: We go over the Week 7 NFL injury report, providing updates and fantasy football analysis.
articles.body:
We're almost at the midway point of 2026 and it feels like the injury report is stabilizing a bit. We had a slew of injured players pop up early in the season, and while the report this week feels lighter, we still have plenty of players to monitor for fantasy football. Let's go over all the latest news and updates for the Week 7 NFL injury report.

Jalen Hurts, PHI (blood clots) — Reportedly out for season

Jackson : The Ravens QB has missed the past two games due to an ankle injury. Tyler Huntley has filled in and the offense has mostly been a mixed bag — good result in Week 5 against the Falcons, rough one against the Browns this past week. Jackson should have a shot at returning this week against the Bengals, providing a nice boost to the offense overall, most notably WR Zay Flowers and TE Mark Andrews.

Hurts : Reports came out Monday morning that the Eagles QB is expected to miss the rest of season as he works to recover from blood clots in his lungs. With Hurts sidelined, Philly turned to Tanner McKee in the loss to Carolina in Week 6. He finished with 215 yards and one TD for 12.6 fantasy points. Fortunately, he was able to keep DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert afloat for fantasy managers, but the upside is clearly lacking. Saquon Barkley's eventual return will help and the Eagles have a pretty soft schedule until later in the year. Still, i t's going to be tough to trust this unit for fantasy moving forward .

Mayfield : Tampa Bay may be getting its starter back in the fold soon. Reports over the weekend suggest Mayfield could be back in Week 7 against the Panthers. Mayfield pushed to play this past week in the loss to Pittsburgh, but Jalon Daniels got another start, finishing with 164 yards, 1 TD, 2 INTs and 39 rushing yards. Similar to the Eagles' situation, the Bucs' offensive upside is capped with a backup QB. Once Mayfield returns we can reassess things, considering the team didn't look great early in the season.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, WAS (groin) — Placed on IR

Jordan Mason, RB, MIN (thumb) — Could come off IR this week

Josh Jacobs, GB — Off the Commissioner's Exempt List

Zach Charbonnet, SEA (knee) — Could come off PUP list this week

Barkley : Philly's lead back has been out the past two games nursing a hamstring injury. The Eagles desperately need his services given Hurts is not expected to be back this season. With Barkley (and Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley out), the Eagles turned to Dameon Pierce, who got all the work out of the backfield in Week 6 against the Panthers. He finished with just 35 yards on 12 carries, but scored a TD (13 fantasy points) to get home for managers. If Barkley remains out, Pierce won't be a bad flex play against Dallas in Week 7. If Barkley is back, expect a heavy workload with McKee under center.

Love : The rookie was ruled out for Week 6. With Love still feeling the effects of an ankle injury, the Cardinals are clearly being cautious with the first-round back. With Love sidelined, Arizona turned to Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight against the Rams on Sunday. The duo combined for 32 carries, three catches and 146 total yards (28 receiving). Knight was the more effective rusher with 80 yards on the ground. He's going to be a trendy pickup this week, though we could see Love back in Week 7 against the Broncos. If Love remains out, both Knight and Allgeier are flex plays at best.

Davante Adams, LAR (hamstring) — Out 6-10 weeks

Mike Evans, SF (Achilles) — Expected to miss some time

Terry McLaurin, WAS (knee) — Out for the year after tearing his patellar tendon

Romeo Doubs, NE (shoulder) — Placed on IR

Tank Dell, HOU (knee) — On track to return Week 7

Evans : The veteran wideout was forced to exit MNF against the Commanders with Achilles soreness and did not return . He posted three catches on five targets for 94 yards before exiting. The Niners are also down Deebo Samuel Sr., among other WRs already out. Evans is going for more testing but the expectation is he'll miss some time. The 49ers face the Falcons in Week 7 before the Week 8 bye. If Evans is out, expect Kyle Shanahan to use Christian McCaffrey, Kaelon Black and George Kittle primarily. WRs Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing and Brandin Cooks split snaps on MNF. None of them did much and it would be tough to predict if any of them would provide fantasy value outside of a weak flex option in deep PPR formats.

McLaurin : Terry suffered a scary injury, and the worst was confirmed on Tuesday when it was reported he tore his patellar tendon, ending his 2026 season. He was carted off during MNF against the Niners due to the injury. With McLaurin out, the Commanders are set to focus the passing game on Stefon Diggs, Chig Okonkwo and rookie Antonio Williams. Treylon Burks also figures to get more snaps/targets; he had 4-66-0 on Monday. Williams and Okonkwo are proactive pickups off the waiver wire for Week 7 despite Washington being on bye.

Adams : Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday afternoon that Adams is expected to miss 6-10 weeks due to a ruptured hamstring . Adams is set to undergo surgery on his hamstring. It's a tough break for the Rams, who are already struggling at 2-4 this season. Puka Nacua has always thrived with Adams off the field as L.A. likes using 13-personnel often. Nacua was already elite for fantasy but we could see ceiling games more often now. Tight ends Tyler Higbee and Terrance Ferguson (currently on IR) aren't bad adds off the waiver wire, while Konata Mumpfield is a risky flex option. Be on the lookout for the Rams to potentially add a wideout via trade as well.

Warren : The Colts added Warren to the injury report later in Week 6 and he was ruled out for the loss to Tennessee. As a result, Indy went with a three-man rotation at TE, split between Mo-Alie Cox, Drew Ogletree and Will Mallory. Cox caught a goal-line TD pass while Mallory had two catches for 20 yards. Daniel Jones and the passing game continue to struggle, so even when Warren is back, he's more of a low-end TE1 who is TD dependent.

articles.title: La jugada de estrategia del Deportivo Pasto que se ha vuelto viral en todo el mundo: “¡Juguemos en el bosque!”
articles.standfirst: La insólita jugada viral del Deportivo Pasto que causa risas a nivel mundial
articles.summary: La insólita jugada viral del Deportivo Pasto que causa risas a nivel mundial
articles.body: El fútbol colombiano volvió a acaparar los reflectores internacionales, pero esta vez no precisamente por una genialidad táctica o un gol de antología, sino por una hilarante y desconcertante jugada preparada que protagonizó el Deportivo Pasto en su duelo frente a Alianza F.C. por la Liga BetPlay. Corría el minuto 53 del encuentro disputado en el Estadio Departamental Libertad. El conjunto ‘volcánico’, que atraviesa un momento complejo en el torneo, dispuso de un tiro de esquina a favor con la urgencia de encontrar el empate. Sin embargo, lo que se gestó en el área rival dejó perplejos a los defensas contrarios, a los hinchas y al propio narrador de la transmisión oficial. En lugar de los tradicionales bloqueos o diagonales típicas de una jugada de laboratorio, varios futbolistas del Pasto comenzaron a dar vueltas en círculo dentro del área chica, simulando una ronda infantil. La escena fue tan surrealista que el relator del partido no dudó en musicalizar el momento al aire con la clásica ronda infantil: “Juguemos en el bosque, a ver si el lobo está... ¿Lobo estás?”. La innovadora (y bizarra) táctica buscaba descolocar por completo la marcación zonal e individual de Alianza, generando confusión en la zaga defensiva. No obstante, el resultado estuvo lejos de ser el esperado: la ejecución posterior del cobro de esquina careció de precisión, el balón se fue lejos y toda la puesta en escena quedó en anécdota viral. Las imágenes no tardaron en expandirse a través de las redes sociales y portales deportivos de diferentes países, catalogando la acción como una de las "técnicas prohibidas" más insólitas vistas en un campo de juego profesional. Más allá de la sonrisa y los memes que dejó la jugada alrededor del mundo, la realidad del Deportivo Pasto en el rentado nacional agobia a su afición. La derrota por 0-1 ante Alianza (con el tanto anotado por Israel Alba y la posterior expulsión de Déinner Quiñones) dejó al cuadro nariñense en una situación crítica en la tabla de posiciones, complicando seriamente sus aspiraciones de clasificación. Los hinchas pastusos habrán de esperar que el ingenio de su equipo se traduzca pronto en victorias reales sobre el césped, mientras tanto, su creativa ronda de "juguemos en el bosque" ya quedó grabada en el apartado de los momentos más insólitos de la historia reciente del FPC.

articles.title: Escándalo en el FPC: 25 árbitros habrían adulterado exámenes médicos
articles.standfirst: El hecho pone en entredicho nuevamente al gremio arbitral en Colombia
articles.summary: El hecho pone en entredicho nuevamente al gremio arbitral en Colombia
articles.body: Una nueva y grave polémica sacude los cimientos del fútbol profesional colombiano. En medio de un entorno ya vigilado por constantes cuestionamientos sobre el arbitraje, se conoció que un grupo de 25 árbitros del país habrían adulterado sus exámenes médicos, motivo por el cual recibieron drásticas sanciones. La información, revelada inicialmente por el diario La Patria, pone nuevamente bajo la lupa los procesos de control, transparencia y selección a los que se somete el cuerpo arbitral en Colombia. Los exámenes médicos y físicos son un requisito obligatorio y fundamental para garantizar que los jueces se encuentran en óptimas condiciones de salud y rendimiento para afrontar las altas exigencias del rentado nacional. Sin embargo, la investigación apunta a que este grupo de 25 jueces habría recurrido a la adulteración de dichos documentos o pruebas, violentando los protocolos éticos y reglamentarios establecidos por las autoridades competentes. Este tipo de irregularidades no solo representa una falta grave a los reglamentos internos del arbitraje y la ley deportiva, sino que también pone en entredicho la equidad y la confianza en la competición, dado que el estado físico y clínico de un juez es vital para el correcto desarrollo de los partidos de la Liga. El arbitraje colombiano ha estado en el centro del debate público en los últimos tiempos debido a errores polémicos en cancha, cuestionamientos desde el sistema VAR y denuncias sobre manejos internos. Este nuevo episodio de presunta falsificación o manipulación de exámenes médicos añade una capa de gravedad institucional, exigiendo respuestas claras por parte de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol (FCF) y la Comisión Arbitral Nacional. Se espera que en los próximos días se conozcan más detalles oficiales sobre las medidas disciplinarias específicas contra cada uno de los implicados, así como los nombres de los jueces cobijados por estas sanciones, en un esfuerzo por limpiar la imagen del gremio y garantizar transparencia de cara al desarrollo del campeonat

articles.title: Luis Díaz supera a Bellingham y Messi en la previa del Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: El colombiano figura entre los favoritos para entrar al Top 10 del galardón
articles.summary: El colombiano figura entre los favoritos para entrar al Top 10 del galardón
articles.body: A pocos días de la gran gala del Balón de Oro, que se celebrará este lunes 26 de octubre en Londres, el nombre del colombiano Luis Díaz vuelve a acaparar los titulares de la prensa internacional. Según las proyecciones y análisis de medios especializados como The Athletic, el extremo nacional se ubica en el octavo puesto del ranking mundial, superando a figuras de la talla del inglés Jude Bellingham y del argentino Lionel Messi. Esta es la segunda vez que el guajiro integra la prestigiosa lista de nominados al galardón, mejorando notablemente las sensaciones respecto a su primera aparición en 2022 (cuando ocupó la casilla 17). El ascenso de Lucho Díaz en las votaciones de los 100 periodistas internacionales no es casualidad. Su rendimiento en la temporada con el Bayern Múnich fue determinante para colocarlo en el Top 10. El delantero colombiano formó parte de la ofensiva más temida de Europa, ayudando a que el conjunto bávaro firmara registros impresionantes —como los 184 goles anotados en 55 partidos oficiales—. En el plano individual, Díaz ratificó su olfato goleador y su capacidad de asistidor: firmó 22 goles e incrementó de forma notable su registro de pases de gol (17), superando los números de su anterior nominación. La prensa internacional le reconoce no solo sus cifras anotadoras, sino también su constante despliegue físico y su rol fundamental para potenciar el juego en equipo junto a socios de peso como Harry Kane y Michael Olise. Estar en la octava posición le permite al colombiano superar a pesos pesados de este deporte: El único punto bajo señalado en el balance del colombiano fue su participación con la Selección Colombia en la cita mundialista, donde su aporte se limitó a un gol y una asistencia, un factor que le impidió escalar aún más alto en la pelea por los lugares de honor (donde nombres como Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal y Kylian Mbappé lideran las principales apuestas). Aunque el podio final estará reservado para los máximos dominadores del año futbolístico, la presencia de Luis Díaz en el Top 8 mundial ratifica su consolidación definitiva en la élite del balompié internacional. El próximo lunes, el mundo del deporte pondrá sus ojos en Londres para conocer los resultados definitivos de una temporada en la que el talento colombiano volvió a brillar en lo más alto del planeta.

articles.title: Top Texas school's star QB ruled ineligible, but playoffs still in reach
articles.summary: A residency dispute sidelines one of Texas's best quarterbacks, but can the team keep winning without him?
articles.body:
Another one of the best high school football teams in the state of Texas just lost their star quarterback.

The Argyle Eagles , the state's No. 5-ranked team in Class 5A Division II by the Houston Chronicle, have won seven of their first eight games, including a perfect 4-0 district record. UIL's District 3 5A-II Executive Committee (DEC), which oversees Argyle, ruled Tuesday that the Eagles used an ineligible player.

However, unlike a similar ruling against the Lewisville Fighting Farmers , this one will not result in a forfeiture of victories.

Hayes Hackney, a junior transfer quarterback from Prosper Walnut Grove, has been one of the best quarterbacks in Texas. Hackney, who currently has offers from UTSA and Stephen F. Austin, has thrown for 2,574 passing yards and 32 touchdown passes in eight games.

The DEC initially ruled Hackney eligible at a May hearing on his residency after transferring from Prosper Walnut Grove, but the Eagles quarterback is now prohibited from playing for the rest of the season after the latest hearing. It's not clear what new evidence was presented to change the DEC's ruling.

According to Greg Riddle of the Dallas Morning News , Hackney's father stated they plan to appeal the ruling to the UIL. The Eagles have only two regular-season games left before their postseason journey begins.

In September, another transfer quarterback was ruled ineligible, which forced the Fighting Farmers to vacate three wins after the DEC found that Laykon Brassfield did not actually reside in Lewisville. The ruling's discipline was harsh, making Brassfield ineligible for varsity competition for one calendar year from the date he enrolled in the high school.

While Brassfield has been off the team, the Fighting Farmers have won every game since the ruling, with a 4-3 record and a likely shot at clinching a postseason berth.

Argyle will likely turn to sophomore quarterback Cobe Wilson, who has played limited snaps as a backup, mostly when the game has been out of reach. According to MaxPreps, Wilson has thrown for 82 yards and a touchdown while rushing for 78 yards and a touchdown in six games. Wilson has also seen time at receiver, with two receptions, 38 receiving yards and one touchdown.

articles.title: IRSC proposes eliminating championship swim, dive programs
articles.summary: IRSC could eliminate its swimming and diving programs, whose men and women have combined for 100 consecutive NJCAA national championships.
articles.body:
Despite a decades-long string of national championships unmatched across college sports, Indian River State College's swimming and diving programs could soon cease to exist.

The IRSC Board of Trustees is scheduled to consider eliminating the Pioneers' dynastic swimming and diving programs at its Oct. 27 meeting. The proposal was recommended by President Tom Moore as part of the school's Athletic Restructuring Plan.

Indian River State's men have won 52 consecutive NJCAA national championships while the women have captured 48 consecutive national titles.

The meeting is scheduled for 9:30 a.m. Tuesday, Oct. 27, at the Williamson Conference Center Auditorium on IRSC's Dixon Hendry campus in Okeechobee.

If approved, the swimming and diving programs would be eliminated by the start of the 2027-28 academic year.

Also on the agenda is a proposal to move IRSC's softball, men's basketball and baseball programs to NJCAA Division II, where the school's volleyball team competes.

The administration also will evaluate the feasibility of reinstating women's basketball for the 2028-29 academic year. IRSC eliminated the program in 2024 .

This is a developing story. Check back for updates.

articles.title: 'Coach Ted' keeps cross country runners moving for 50 years
articles.summary: Coach Ted has a long-running legacy, having spent time as a teacher, coach, and now PIAA official at William Tennent High School.
articles.body:
Coach Ted Abel has a long-running legacy, having spent time as a teacher, coach, and now PIAA official over the past half-century at William Tennent High School.

He started teaching in 1973 and then started coaching track and field in 1974. He then added cross country to his repertoire the year after.

But even before that, Abel was a student down the road at Upper Moreland High School. There, he competed in the annual William Tennent Cross Country Invitational.

It's that very invitational that he has kept moving over the years.

However, the event encountered a few speed bumps in its seven-decade history. In the 1980s, it was even threatened by a similar event taking place at the same time.

But Abel, his fellow coaches, and the broader William Tennent community refused to allow the event to peter out.

Now, it attracts hundreds of students from dozens of area schools who zig and zag through a course full of varied elevations.

That very course is known as the Coach Ted Abel Cross Country Course.

Abel hopes to continue serving as a PIAA official as long as he's having fun.

Watch the video above to see the story in action.

You could say he's on a roll at 100 years old. William Owen Hanna is a veteran, a deacon, and a lifelong bowler who still hits the lanes every week.
